sections.h2: Where deeds are filed and until what hour
sections.html:
Houghton County deeds go to the courthouse in the city of Houghton, second floor, 401 E. Houghton Avenue (ZIP 49931). Call 906-482-1311. Staff are in from 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, yet the recording day closes at 3:30, so a deed delivered after 3:30 misses that day's recording.

The Register of Deeds page on the county site describes the office's job: keeping an index plus a copy of every recorded instrument tied to land here. The shelves hold deeds, mortgages, plats, surveys, land corners and a miscellaneous category. Anyone with a nagging boundary question can request the survey or the land corner record for the parcel before the listing goes live.

sections.h2: What the courthouse charges to file a deed
sections.html:
One flat $30.00 covers a document of any length. The figure already includes the state remonumentation charge and the register automation charge. Make the check out to the office by name. The fee comes from MCL 600.2567.

  • Add $3.00 for every instrument beyond the first named in an assignment or discharge.
  • Add $5.00 when a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract or land contract assignment is certified.
  • Copies of real estate records are priced by the page at $1.00, and plat copies at $2.00.
  • A lien certificate search, state or federal, runs $3.00 for each name.

Transfer tax is billed separately and is not part of any of these numbers.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Houghton County closing
sections.html:
Michigan stacks a state tax and a county tax on the sales price. The county half, set at 55 cents in counties under two million people by MCL 207.504, governs here because Houghton County has under 40,000 residents. The deed must show the full consideration, or a sworn statement of value must ride along with it. Your title company will work out the total and collect it at closing.

Charges on a Houghton County deed
ChargeRateStatute
State transfer tax$3.75 for each $500 or part of $500MCL 207.525
County transfer tax$0.55 for each $500 or part of $500MCL 207.504
Recording$30.00 flatMCL 600.2567

Some transfers escape the state tax under MCL 207.526:

  • Paper that carries consideration below $100.
  • A deed delivered through foreclosure or in place of it.
  • Court-ordered transfers where the judge sets no price.
  • A gift deed to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • A land contract, until title actually moves to the buyer.

The county statute's exemption list, MCL 207.505, contains no child or grandchild entry. Ask the office how the county portion works for a family deed.

sections.h2: Formatting mistakes that get a deed bounced
sections.html:
Under MCL 565.201 the register must refuse paper that breaks the layout rules. Check the draft against this list before it leaves your hands:

  • Black or dark blue ink for signatures, with a printed name under each one.
  • A grantee mailing address, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A blank strip of 2.5 inches across the top of page one and half an inch elsewhere.
  • 10 point type or larger, on white stock of 20 pounds or heavier, sized 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • One opening line naming the single recordable event.
  • Social Security numbers cut to the last four digits, and any foreign language text translated.

Once a conforming instrument is in, the statute bars the register from refusing it over its content.

sections.h2: Can a deed be filed or searched without driving to the courthouse?
sections.html:
Yes on both counts. Four vendors send electronic filings here: CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Indecomm. They may submit at any hour, and the office works the queue between 8:30 and 3:30. The county advertises same day recording and fewer lost papers, while warning that some document types cannot go electronic.

For searching, the county points to Tapestry, an occasional-user tool covering September 1993 to the present. A search costs $8.75, viewing images is free and each printed page is $1.00. Professionals who search constantly can subscribe to Laredo. The in-office tract index is billed at $400.00 a month, $20.00 an hour or $5.00 per quarter hour. Owners can also enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert, which pings them when their exact name shows up on a newly recorded paper.

sections.h2: Old titles and parcels in the Copper Country
sections.html:
The mining boom drew people from dozens of countries, and a name search on a very old Houghton County deed is worth running under several spellings. Raise that with the title company early.

The land itself has changed too. In June 2018 a flash flood left sinkholes and washouts in Chassell, Houghton, Ripley, Lake Linden and Hubbell. A seller in one of those places should gather repair invoices and permits and keep them with the sale file, since a buyer will ask what was fixed.

sections.h2: County desks that handle taxes before a sale
sections.html:
The Treasurer is on the courthouse second floor too, at 906-482-0560, and keeps the same weekday schedule of 8:00 to 4:30. That desk collects delinquent real estate tax, certifies deeds and plats, prints tax histories and arranges partial payment plans. It also hosts the tax sale and foreclosure timeline pages.

Equalization supports 16 assessing jurisdictions and sends their taxable values to the State Tax Commission annually. Write to equalization@houghtoncounty.net or to Attn: Equalization, 401 E Houghton Ave, Houghton MI 49931. Calling the Treasurer ahead of closing shows the title company whether anything is owed.

sections.h2: Steps for a seller at the courthouse
sections.html: First, get the signed deed from your attorney or title agent and check it against the layout list above. Second, ask the Treasurer whether the parcel has any unpaid tax and whether a warranty deed needs the $5.00 certification. Third, bring the check for recording and the transfer tax, or let the title company e-file. Arrive before 3:30 if you are delivering paper, because a later deed waits for the next recording day. Keep the stamped copy once it is returned.

The county covers 1,502 square miles of the Keweenaw Peninsula and has about 37,842 residents by the 2025 estimate. Houghton is the county seat, and Michigan Technological University is in the county. Owners live in 71.8 percent of the 19,308 housing units. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $159,900, and the typical rent is $840.

faqs.q: How much is the deed filing fee at Houghton County?
faqs.a: A single $30.00 charge applies no matter how long the document is. A $5.00 certification is added for warranty deeds and land contracts, and $3.00 for each further instrument in an assignment or discharge.

faqs.q: Is 3:30 really the last call for recording in Houghton?
faqs.a: Yes. Doors stay open until 4:30 p.m., though the day's recording ends at 3:30 p.m. E-files may arrive overnight and get worked during the 8:30 to 3:30 window.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when a Houghton County home is sold?
faqs.a: Ask the title company or the register how your contract assigns it. The rates are $3.75 state plus $0.55 county for each $500, due when the deed is submitted.

faqs.q: Is there a way to look up Houghton deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. Tapestry has records from September 1993 forward at $8.75 a search with free image viewing, and Laredo suits frequent searchers. For earlier material, call 906-482-1311.

faqs.q: Whom do I ask about back taxes on a Houghton parcel?
faqs.a: The Treasurer at 906-482-0560, courthouse second floor, is the contact. The desk handles delinquent taxes, tax histories, payment plans and tax sale information.
